subject: Rivernova private-offer MAP + eval schedule and invoice routing
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@rivernova.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@rivernova.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Rivernova MAP & private-offer details (initial)

Hi Kimberly + Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is keen to move forward with a private offer on AWS. Procurement asked me to share a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and the priority acceptance criteria for our technical eval. I attached a short draft to this message.

High-level asks from Rivernova:
- 2-week production-like eval window (approx 10k tokens/day)
- SOC2 evidence and data residency confirmation for logs
- Standard AWS private-offer flow + invoicing to our finance team (Maya copied)

Could you confirm whether the proposed MAP timeline is feasible and what the invoice routing steps will look like for a Marketplace private-offer?

Attachment: rivernova_mpa_v1.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Alex Chen
Director of ML Platform
Rivernova
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@rivernova.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rivernova MAP & private-offer details (initial)

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the MAP draft. I reviewed the attachment and sketched a practical eval plan that mirrors your acceptance criteria. Key notes below and attached: kpark_eval_plan_20270412.xlsx.

Summary (we can update during a quick sync):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): sandbox creds, autogenerated test dataset, and access to a dedicated dev slot on our AWS private-offer pool.
- Week 1 (Smoke + performance): latency and cost profiling at 512/2k seq. We will snapshot token-level cost and latency.
- Week 2 (Prod-like run): your 10k tokens/day pattern; we’ll enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Acceptance gates: functional correctness (sample prompts), 95th percentile latency <= 450ms, and budget alerting configured.

Invoice/routing notes:
- For AWS private-offer the invoice flows through Marketplace invoicing by default; if Rivernova requires direct invoicing to Maya, we can request an invoice override during the private-offer creation (requires AWS paperwork + billing contact).
- Practical path we recommend: Marketplace PO -> Redwood issues invoice to Marketplace -> Marketplace pays Redwood -> Redwood issues customer-facing invoice (copy to procurement@rivernova.com) for internal reconciliation.

I’m looping Jonas to confirm whether the invoice override is likely to add 7–10 business days to the close. If you'd like, we can run the MAP with Marketplace-standard invoicing to avoid delays and provide a separate reconciliation statement for your finance team.

Attachments: kpark_eval_plan_20270412.xlsx

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex@rivernova.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rivernova MAP & private-offer details (initial)

Alex / Kimberly — quick note on billing:

If Rivernova requires the invoice to list Rivernova as the remitter and route a PO directly to Redwood (i.e., not solely via Marketplace settlement), we will need the AWS private-offer to be configured with an invoice override. That path typically requires:
- Signed Marketplace private-offer form + legal contact
- Redwood billing team to set up alternate remit instructions (we will request this internally)
- Accounting lead (Maya) to confirm tax details and purchase order number

Estimated impact to timeline: add ~7 business days for the billing override to be processed. If timing is tight, Kimberly's suggestion to use standard Marketplace settlement and provide a reconciliation ledger is the lowest friction.

I’ll prepare a short checklist and the invoice-routing guidance PDF and share it here.

Attachment: invoice-routing-guidance.pdf

—Jonas
Director, Revenue Ops
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@rivernova.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rivernova MAP & private-offer details (initial)

Alex — quick operational confirm from my side:
- We can provision the dev slot tomorrow (Tue) if you share the test service account and an example prompt corpus by EOD Monday.
- I’ll enable alerting hooks for budget and latency and share the dashboards link.

If you prefer a 30-minute kickoff instead of back-and-forth, I can do 10:30am PDT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Grace O’Connor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex@rivernova.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@rivernova.com>, Maya Singh <maya@rivernova.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rivernova MAP & private-offer details (initial)

Team — this all looks good. We’ll proceed with the Marketplace-standard invoicing to avoid the billing override delay. Two quick asks before we kick off the MAP Tuesday:
1) Kimberly — can you confirm the exact dev slot name and IAM principal we should send logs from so data residency is preserved?
2) Jonas — please send the short checklist for what Procurement needs to include in the PO (billing address, tax id, PO number format).

Procurement will issue a PO today and Maya will upload tax docs once we have the PO format. Looking forward to the kickoff.

—Alex
